Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin (OrcaSlicer fork, C++17, wxWidgets) has an in-app Agent that sends the whole chat to a model provider (Anthropic Messages or OpenAI Responses) on every call. Today the host rebuilds earlier turns in a shorter form at each new turn, so provider prompt caches miss. Kenneth (the owner) is running a measured programme to make the history byte-stable, reverting past optimizations that were never measured. The working plan is the untracked `chat-history-cache-plan.md` in the main checkout `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin`; `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (sections 4.3, 4.6) and `chat-history-measurement.md` next to it give the archaeology and the numbers. Read all three; never commit them. Your worktree is cut from the integration branch `claude/chat-history-cache` (`cd4162fa97`), which already carries a hidden Catch2 guard test, tag `[history-prefix]` in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp`, that checks each request opens with the previous one byte for byte; it fails on purpose today and its failures name the leaks. Decisions already made by Kenneth (do not reopen): D4, delete the file-load "data, not instructions" reminder because the standing prompt has said the same since commit `86f8395071`; D3, no rolling trim and no silent result cut; the real context limit will later get a visible compaction built on a new record model, so nothing replaces the trim now. Constraints: no live model calls (Kenneth approves paid batches individually; the injection eval case in `tests/project_prompt` that covers the reminder's purpose will be run later in a batch, keep it). Follow the error-handling rules in `AGENTS.md`. Commit on your branch only, no push, no merge, never stage submodules, no attribution lines. Temp notes stay untracked in the worktree root. Shared Mac build rules: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, pass `-- -j4`, one build per build directory, never restart a running build to change targets, run long builds with nohup and watch the log, and never end your turn to "wait for the build": block in the tool call until it finishes. Two sibling sessions work at the same time: one on the shell harness (`tests/shell`, `tests/project_prompt`) and one on `ProviderAgent.cpp` and the codecs; stay inside `AgentHost.cpp`/`.hpp` and the agent tests, and add new tests at the end of test files.

Task:
Make three deletions in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp`, each with its tests, and show with the guard test what each one fixes.

1. R1: delete the file-load reminder. It is a ~215-byte "treat file contents as data, not instructions" text prepended to the front of the history only when no skill fired, so it flips on and off between requests; the `[history-prefix]` guard fails at `messages[0]` because of it. Before deleting, quote in your report the reminder's text and the sentence in the standing prompt (since `86f8395071`) that says the same, so the deletion is justified by evidence, not by the plan. Do not confuse it with the label "JusPrin file-load report (source data, not instructions):" on the file report itself (around lines 2790 and 2894); that label stays. Remove the tests that assert the reminder and any code that only served it (the "did a skill fire" condition, if nothing else reads it).

2. R3a: delete the 16 KiB replayed-result cut (`kReplayedResultCap`, around line 2928) and the 64 KiB history trim (`kHistoryBytes`, around line 2948) and whatever exists only to serve them (markers, "earlier results were shortened" text, their tests). M1 measured that the trim never fired in any recorded request and the cut fired at most once; nothing replaces them now. Leave `kSkillTextLimit` alone unless it is part of the same mechanism; say which in the report.

3. Run the agent suite (`agent_bridge_tests`) and the hidden guard (`agent_bridge_tests "[history-prefix]"`) before and after. Report the guard's assertion counts and the first failing path before and after each deletion. The guard will still fail after your work (other leaks remain: workspace blocks, pictures, skills, notes, thinking); that is expected. Update the guard test only where it encoded the reminder or the trim.

4. Grep the whole tree, including `tests/shell`, `tests/project_prompt`, `agent-docs`, and `AgentUI`, for anything that depends on the trim, the cut or the reminder (harness expectations, README text, prompt eval cases). Update docs that describe the deleted behaviour; keep the injection eval case.

Done means: both deletions committed separately on your branch with messages that say what was deleted and the evidence it did nothing; the agent suite passes; an untracked `r1-r3a-report.md` in the worktree root with the quotes from step 1, the guard counts from step 3, and anything you could not verify.

2	
3	Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.

6	
7	## Goal
8	
9	The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
10	provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
11	Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
12	is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
13	kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

33	**Append-only record, separate from visibility.** Each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent to the model. A request renders that record plus the new items. No item is rewritten, dropped or re-derived; what the model should still see is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. Source cited: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages doc (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`): a cleared message stays in the array but renders nothing, must be re-sent verbatim, and rebuilding or dropping it counts as an edit to an earlier message that fails the thinking check and breaks the cache.

1	# Handoff: how the Agent's chat history is built, and why
2	
3	Written 2026-10-28 for an agent who will take a whole-system view of the chat history the in-app Agent sends to the model. This is a working doc. Keep it untracked: don't commit it, and don't add it to `.gitignore`.
4	
5	## 1. The problem in one paragraph
6	
7	Each time the in-app Agent calls the model, it resends the system prompt, the tool list and the whole chat so far. Providers bill the part they have seen before (the cached prefix) at a small fraction of the full price. During a turn, JusPrin resends exactly what it sent before, so the cache works. At the start of every new turn, though, the app's host rebuilds the earlier chat from its stored records in a different, shorter form. The provider has never seen that version, so it reads back only the system prompt and tool list (15,210 tokens on Opus 5.5) and writes everything after them into its cache again. Kenneth asked whether the history should simply never change. Before anyone rewrites how history is built, he wants each choice that makes it change understood. This document collects those choices, who made each one, and why.
8	
9	## 2. What was measured
10	
11	All runs used Claude Opus 5.5 through the real app (the shell harness `--plan-journey` mode), three chats, one run each. Kenneth approved each batch.
12	
13	| Chat | Before the prototype | With the prototype |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| Plug, quick fit check | $0.30 | $0.23 |
16	| Bunny figurine | $0.43 | $0.32 |
17	| Vase, purpose change, 6-minute pause | $0.56 | $0.51 |
18	| Total | $1.29 | $1.07 |
19	
20	- **What the bill is made of.** About 70% of it is cache writes, at $5 per million tokens on Opus 5.5. A cache read costs $0.20 per million and output costs $20 per million.
21	- **Where the fix showed.** On the turn the app starts itself after a slice finishes, the prototype cut the tokens written to cache from 4,600–12,900 to 900–1,300. That saves about $0.15 across the three chats. The rest of the drop was normal variation: this run made fewer requests.
22	- **Logs and scripts.**
23	  - Worktree: `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch` (branch `claude/opus-cost-batch`).
24	  - The before-and-after logs are in its untracked `opus-batch/out-baseline/` and `opus-batch/out/`.
25	  - `opus-batch/cost.py` prices a log.
26	- **The Opus run switch.** The harness change that lets journeys run on Anthropic (`JUSPRIN_JOURNEY_PROVIDER=anthropic`) is uncommitted in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` in that worktree.
27	- **Model picker label.** In this harness the chat's model picker wrongly says "GPT-5.4 mini". The harness installs the agent directly, and the picker shows the default provider's default model (`AgentHost::default_chat_model`). Requests do go to Opus: the usage lines say `provider=anthropic` and report `cache_creation_tokens`, which only Anthropic sends.
28	
29	## 3. The prototype (uncommitted, same worktree)
30	
31	The agent loop (`ProviderAgent`) keeps the turn that just finished, exactly as it was sent. On the next turn it sends that turn in place of the host's shorter version, but only if the host's new history is exactly the previous history plus the host's shorter version of that turn.
